questions.question: Within what percentage of rated capacity does a crane lift need a second qualified person to confirm the load?
questions.expected_answer: Lifts within 90 percent of rated capacity.

questions.question: Who directs the crane operator during a lift?
questions.expected_answer: One designated signal person, using standard hand signals or a two-way radio.

questions.question: How recently must rigging hardware have been inspected before it may be used?
questions.expected_answer: Within the last 12 months, and it must be rated for the intended load.

questions.question: What happens to a sling that shows cuts, abrasion or crushed fibers?
questions.expected_answer: It is removed from service on the spot.
keywords: removed from service on the spot

questions.question: What must the crane operator do if radio contact with the signal person is lost during a lift?
questions.expected_answer: Hold the load in place until visual signal contact is reestablished.

questions.question: How large must the exclusion zone radius around a suspended load be?
questions.expected_answer: At least the maximum boom length.

questions.question: What does the crane operator check before any lift?
questions.expected_answer: The hoist line for fraying, that the load chart matches the boom configuration, the upper and lower limit switches, and that outrigger pads are on stable, level ground.

questions.question: When is a crane lift treated as a critical lift, and what does it require?
questions.expected_answer: When the load weight is uncertain; it needs a written lift plan reviewed by the site safety officer beforehand.

questions.question: What happens to a crane that has a damaged hook latch?
questions.expected_answer: It is a safety-critical defect, so the crane is tagged out of service immediately.

questions.question: When must riggers attach a tag line to a load?
questions.expected_answer: To any load that could rotate or swing once it clears the ground.

questions.question: Which factors determine the choice of sling for a lift?
questions.expected_answer: The load weight, the center of gravity and the angle of the lift - never estimated by eye.

questions.question: What must the crane operator and the signal person agree on before the lift begins?
questions.expected_answer: That they use the same signal set, and an emergency stop signal that overrides all other instructions.

questions.question: When can the exclusion zone barriers be removed after a lift?
questions.expected_answer: Once the load is set down, the rigging is slack and the signal person confirms the area is clear.

questions.question: The boom length changed since the last lift. Can the operator reuse the capacity from that previous lift?
questions.expected_answer: No. Rated capacity changes with boom angle, boom length and counterweight, so the load chart must be consulted for every new lift.
keywords: load chart for every new lift

questions.question: A worker dropped a tool under a suspended load. May they walk under it to pick the tool up?
questions.expected_answer: No. No one may walk under a suspended load for any reason, including to retrieve dropped tools.

questions.question: Why must outrigger pads be on stable, level ground before the boom is extended?
questions.expected_answer: Because an unstable base is one of the leading causes of tip-over incidents on mobile cranes.

questions.question: Who has to stop work during a severe weather warning, and who directs a crane lift?
questions.expected_answer: Forklift and crane operations stop immediately; a single designated signal person directs crane lifts.

questions.question: What is the maximum lifting capacity of the crane in tonnes?
